t: Its author and date are debated: the oldest excavated fragments, the Guodian bamboo slips, date to around 300 BCE, and a relatively complete text probably existed by the mid third century BCE.
It describes the Tao as the root of all things and urges a return to harmony with it through wu wei, simplicity and humility, in laconic, paradoxical verse.
Central to philosophical and religious Taoism, it was reread by Legalists, Confucians and Chinese Buddhists, and is one of the most translated texts in world literature.
dyk: The two silk copies found at Mawangdui in 1973 put the Te Ching before the Tao Ching, reversing the traditional order, so one English translation of them is titled Te-Tao Ching.
ev: The Guodian bamboo slips, the oldest known version of the text, are written
The tomb at Mawangdui that held two nearly complete silk copies is dated to this year
The title Tao Te Ching, marking the work as a classic, is first applied under Emperor Jing of Han
Wang Bi writes the commentary behind the most verified of the received editions
Emperor Xuanzong of Tang declares himself an authority on the text, claiming descent from Laozi
John Chalmers publishes the first English translation
Archaeologists recover the Mawangdui Silk Texts
The Guodian Chu slips are found near Guodian in Jingmen, Hubei

f.made: Traditionally ascribed to Laozi, the "Old Master", whose historical existence is debated; most modern scholars hold it to be a compilation of sayings consolidated during the fourth century BCE
f.form: A Classical Chinese text of around 5,162 to 5,450 characters in 81 brief chapters, in two parts, the Tao Ching (chapters 1–37) and the Te Ching (chapters 38–81); about three-quarters rhymed in Old Chinese
f.where: Transmitted in the Yan Zun, Heshang Gong and Wang Bi editions; early manuscripts found at Dunhuang, Mawangdui and Guodian
f.known: The Tao as the source of all existence; wu wei, "non-action"; simplicity and humility; paradox and the limits of language; avoiding war, harsh laws and heavy taxes; foundation of Taoism
